newsitem.title: UK: Minor metals slow in tight ranges, China sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Minor metals slow in tight ranges, China sidelined.

text.p: The minor industrial metals maintained their sideways trading patterns over the past week as major market force China continued New Year celebrations.
"Business is slow overall and is not likely to pick up until next week," one trader commented.
Cobalt failed to react seriously to the ongoing turmoil in Zaire, while indium and gallium against the backdrop of low stocks held steady levels but were showing signs of breaking sharply higher.
Cobalt ingots found some downside pressure from a possible change in major producer Russia's sales strategy and talk that some stockpiled material may be released on to the market this month.
Recently, trade sources said that Russia may be prepared to release some material from strategic metal stockpiles.
They that 420 tonnes of cobalt, 30,000 76 lbs flasks of mercury, 7,000 tonnes of titanium sponge and an undisclosed amount of chrome could be released.
"If - and that is a big if - the metal is released then the relative markets could experience downside pressure," one trader said.
Previous stockpile sales have not always found official permission, the trader explained.
Superalloy and battery demand helped to underpin high grade cobalt which has so far largely ignored the plight of Zaire. Zaire produces around 1,000 tonnes of high grade material a year.
Indium firmed against the backdrop of low Chinese and Russian producer stocks. Traders said that, despite the low inventory levels, consumers have not yet covered in any force.
One trader suggested that indium had the potential to climb to $300 an ounce medium-term.
Indium is used in the electronics industry and in high performance bearings mainly used in sports cars.
Traders reported continued enquiry from Japan.
Gallium was also underpinned by low stock levels from CIS producers. Japanese demand was also noted in gallium.
Elsewhere magnesium was little changed, though traders noted producers continued to run at high levels.
The Chinese holiday dampened enthusiasm in antimony which drifted lower.
